title: Ind-etale refinement of a weakly etale map
statement:
For the construction of [def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement], the map $B\to
B'$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale, and $A\to B'$ is ind-etale.

proof.text:
Use $C,J,D_0$ from [def-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement]. By
[lem-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover], $C/A$ is faithfully flat and ind-etale, and
its maximal local rings are strictly henselian. Since $A	o B$ is weakly etale
and weakly etale maps are stable under base change, $C	o D_0$ is weakly
etale. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] to each fibre of $D_0/C$
shows that its residue fields are algebraic over the base fields. Thus
$T=V(JD_0)$ consists of closed points of $D_0$.
[lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization] makes $B'$ w-local with closed points
$T$, unchanged local rings there, and $D_0\to B'$ ind-Zariski.

At every maximal ideal $n\subset B'$, its contraction $m\subset C$ is
maximal. The composite $C\to D_0\to B'$ is weakly etale: the first map is
the weakly etale base change above, while $D_0\to B'$ is ind-Zariski and
hence ind-etale and weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability].
Therefore the local map $C_m\to B'_n$ is weakly etale, so is an isomorphism
by [thm-weil-pbc-weak-etale-strict-local]. Every prime of $B'$ lies under a
maximal ideal. Localizing this isomorphism again shows that $C\to B'$
identifies all local rings. It is therefore ind-Zariski by
[lem-weil-pbc-local-rings-ind-zariski]. Composition with $A\to C$ proves that
$A\to B'$ is ind-etale.

The map $B\to D_0$ is ind-etale by base change from $A\to C$; composition
makes $B\to B'$ ind-etale and flat as well. The closed point set $V(J)$
surjects onto $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover]. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], the base-changed faithfully flat map remains faithfully flat, so its base change $T$ surjects onto
$\operatorname{Spec}B$, and all these points are retained in
$\operatorname{Spec}B'$. The composite $B	o B'$ is flat, and the retained points give a surjective
map $\operatorname{Spec}B'	o\operatorname{Spec}B$. The existing criterion
[lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] therefore gives
faithful flatness. The construction
gives the refinement theorem commonly formulated in
[Stacks Project, Tag 097Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/097Z); its
covering and local-ring steps have been proved above.
